questions.question: In a game of incomplete information, player $i$ has a type $\theta_i$ from a type space $\Theta_i$, the type profile is $\theta\in\Theta=\Theta_1\times\cdots\times\Theta_n$, and payoffs are $v_i(a;\theta)$. Which parts of this game are common knowledge among the players?
options: The players, actions and every realized type, but not the distribution of types.
The players, actions, type spaces and the distribution of types, but not realized types.
Only each player's own payoff function, since types make all payoffs private.
Nothing beyond the list of players, since every other component may be private.

questions.question: In a normal-form game $\langle N,\{S_i\},\{v_i\}\rangle$ the payoff functions are common knowledge. Which assumption do types relax?
options: Common knowledge of each player's payoffs: uncertainty about them becomes uncertainty about types.
Common knowledge of the players' strategy sets, which become private to each player.
Simultaneity of moves: with types, players move one after another in a fixed order.
Rationality of the players: a type describes how far from rational a player behaves.

questions.question: In a game of incomplete information, player $i$ has a type $\theta_i$ from a type space $\Theta_i$, the type profile is $\theta\in\Theta=\Theta_1\times\cdots\times\Theta_n$, and payoffs are $v_i(a;\theta)$. Player $i$ has action set $A_i$. What is a pure strategy of player $i$?
options: An action $a_i\in A_i$ chosen after she learns her realized type.
A map $s_i\colon\Theta\to A_i$ giving an action for each profile of all players' types.
A map $s_i\colon\Theta_i\to A_i$ giving an action for each of her possible types.
A map $s_i\colon A_i\to\Theta_i$ assigning to each action the type that would choose it.

questions.question: In a game of incomplete information, player $i$ has a type $\theta_i$ from a type space $\Theta_i$, the type profile is $\theta\in\Theta=\Theta_1\times\cdots\times\Theta_n$, and payoffs are $v_i(a;\theta)$. Every player's type space is a singleton, $|\Theta_i|=1$ for all $i$. What kind of game is this?
options: Still a game of incomplete information, since every player has a type.
A game of complete information, since no player has private information.
A game in which only the first player has private information.
A game with no payoffs, since payoffs depend on the types.

questions.question: In a game of incomplete information, player $i$ has a type $\theta_i$ from a type space $\Theta_i$, the type profile is $\theta\in\Theta=\Theta_1\times\cdots\times\Theta_n$, and payoffs are $v_i(a;\theta)$. Player $i$ has three possible types and two actions. How many pure strategies does she have?
In a two-player game of incomplete information, $|\Theta_1|=3$ and $|\Theta_2|=4$. How many type profiles $\theta=(\theta_1,\theta_2)$ are there?

Two neighbours choose $C$ (contribute) or $D$ (decline); a good worth $1$ to each is provided if anyone contributes, and a contributor pays her private cost $\theta_i$. Types are $\theta_1=2$ and $\theta_2=\tfrac{1}{4}$, and the actions are $(C,D)$ (player 1 contributes, player 2 declines). What is player 1's payoff $v_1(a;\theta)$?

Two neighbours choose $C$ (contribute) or $D$ (decline); a good worth $1$ to each is provided if anyone contributes, and a contributor pays her private cost $\theta_i$. Costs are $\theta_i\in\{\tfrac{1}{4},2\}$, and a strategy is written (action of the low-cost type, action of the high-cost type). What does the strategy $(D,C)$ prescribe?
options: Contribute if her cost is $\tfrac{1}{4}$; decline if her cost is $2$.
Decline in the first round and contribute in the second round.
Decline if her cost is $\tfrac{1}{4}$; contribute if her cost is $2$.
Decline herself while requiring the other player to contribute.

questions.question: In a game of incomplete information, player $i$ has a type $\theta_i$ from a type space $\Theta_i$, the type profile is $\theta\in\Theta=\Theta_1\times\cdots\times\Theta_n$, and payoffs are $v_i(a;\theta)$. A seller privately knows the quality $\theta_1$ of her product; a buyer's payoff from buying depends on that quality. Is this consistent with the definition of types?
options: No: a type may affect only its owner's payoff, so the buyer's payoff cannot use $\theta_1$.
No: the buyer's payoff depends on $\theta_1$, so $\theta_1$ must be common knowledge.
Yes, but only if the buyer also observes $\theta_1$ before choosing her action.
Yes: $v_i(a;\theta)$ may depend on the whole profile, including other players' types.

questions.question: In a game of incomplete information, player $i$ has a type $\theta_i$ from a type space $\Theta_i$, the type profile is $\theta\in\Theta=\Theta_1\times\cdots\times\Theta_n$, and payoffs are $v_i(a;\theta)$. Only one type of player $i$ is realized. Why must her strategy still specify an action for every type in $\Theta_i$?
options: Because she does not know her own type until after the game, so she must plan for all.
Because each type is played in a separate round of a repeated game.
The others cannot see $\theta_i$, so they must predict what each possible type would do.
Because a strategy must use every action at least once across the types.

questions.question: A firm privately knows its unit cost $c\in\{1,2\}$ and also privately observes a signal $s\in\{H,L\}$ about market demand, which affects its profit; nothing else about the firm is private. In a game of incomplete information, which type space $\Theta_i$ models the firm's private information?
options: $\Theta_i=\{1,2\}$: a type describes costs and preferences, and a demand signal is not one.
$\Theta_i=\{H,L\}$: the cost is a fixed parameter of the firm, so only the signal is a type.
$\Theta_i=\{1,2\}\cup\{H,L\}$: the firm has one type for each private characteristic.
$\Theta_i=\{1,2\}\times\{H,L\}$: each type is a pair $(c,s)$ of all the firm knows privately.

questions.question: Players 1 and 2 each privately observe a signal $\theta_i\in\{0,1\}$. Player 1 may invest, with payoff $\theta_1+\theta_2-1$, or not, with payoff $0$. She believes $\theta_2=1$ with probability $\tfrac{1}{2}$. Which plan gives each type of player 1 her highest expected payoff?
options: Invest for both types
Invest iff $\theta_1=1$
Invest for neither type
Invest iff $\theta_1=0$

questions.question: In a two-player coordination game, player 2 knows whether she prefers to meet at location $L$ or at $R$, while player 1 does not; player 1's own preferences are known to all. Each player has actions $\{L,R\}$. Modelled with types, how many pure strategies do (player 2, player 1) have?
options: $(4,2)$: player 2 has two types and player 1 a single type
$(2,2)$: preferences are fixed facts, so neither player has types
$(2,4)$: player 1, who is uncertain, gets one type per preference
$(4,4)$: each player gets two types, one per possible preference

questions.question: Two neighbours choose $C$ (contribute) or $D$ (decline); a good worth $1$ to each is provided if anyone contributes, and a contributor pays her private cost $\theta_i$. Player 1's cost is privately $\tfrac{1}{2}$, $\tfrac{3}{2}$ or $\tfrac{5}{2}$. A strategy lists her action for each type. How many of her $8$ pure strategies give no type a strictly dominated action?

Two neighbours choose $C$ (contribute) or $D$ (decline); a good worth $1$ to each is provided if anyone contributes, and a contributor pays her private cost $\theta_i$. Player 1's cost is privately $\tfrac{1}{4}$, $\tfrac{9}{10}$ or $2$, and she believes player 2 contributes with probability $0.2$. Which plan (action for cost $\tfrac{1}{4}$, $\tfrac{9}{10}$, $2$) gives each type her highest expected payoff?

Two neighbours choose $C$ (contribute) or $D$ (decline); a good worth $1$ to each is provided if anyone contributes, and a contributor pays her private cost $\theta_i$. Player 2 does not observe player 1's cost; given her own information she believes it is $\tfrac{1}{4}$ with probability $0.3$ and $2$ with probability $0.7$. Player 1 uses $(C,D)$ (contribute iff her cost is $\tfrac{1}{4}$). With what probability does player 2 expect player 1 to contribute?
A modeller lists private characteristics of player $i$ in a game. Which one is a type of player $i$ in the sense of games of incomplete information?
options: A production cost that has been publicly announced to all players.
A private fact that affects no player's payoff, such as a favourite colour.
The action that player $i$ privately intends to take.
A private signal about a state that enters some player's payoff.

questions.question: In a two-player game of incomplete information, $|\Theta_1|=1$ and $|\Theta_2|=2$, both types of player 2 having positive probability, and player 1's payoff $v_1(a;\theta)$ depends on $\theta_2$. Which statement about player 1 is correct?
options: She has no private information, so she knows all payoffs for certain.
She has private information, because her payoff depends on a type.
Her single type makes the whole game one of complete information.
She has no private information, yet she is uncertain about her own payoffs.
